title: Triangulations and Maximal Cross-Ratio Degrees
summary: The cross-ratio degree problem is about counting rational curves with $n$ marked points satisfying $n-3$ cross-ratio conditions. This problem has a tropical analogue which provides the same number, as shown by a correspondence theorem. In general, there are no closed formulas for this counting problem. In the special case of cross-ratio conditions given by triangulations, a formula was found by Silversmith via techniques of algebraic geometry.
